items.title: AAP, Authors Guild Applaud Decision in ROSS Copyright Infringement Case
items.excerpt: An appeals judge backed a Delaware court ruling that found the now-defunct AI startup’s unauthorized copying of text from Thomson Reuters’s Westlaw platform was not fair use.

items.title: Unsealed Files Show Open AI/Microsoft Knew Copying Was Illegal and Could Hurt Authors
items.excerpt: Newly unsealed comments made in briefs filed by Open AI and Microsoft reveal that executives knew they were illegally training their products on copyrighted books and that AI generated books would likely displace human-authored books in the market.

items.title: OpenAI 'trained models' on books from 'sketchy AF' LibGen, unsealed court filings reveal
items.excerpt: OpenAI staff discussed using books obtained from Library Genesis (LibGen) to train early GPT models, questioned how the source should be described publicly and weighed the cost of buying books instead.

items.title: AI might kill us, but is that so bad?
items.excerpt: While the advent of AI has alarmed most writers, Bonnie Garmus argues it has also shone a light on the hubris of humankind.

items.title: Another AI scandal affects an author in competition for a prestigious award
items.excerpt: Every high-visibility award is at risk of finding itself in this situation if it intends to exclude AI-assisted work from consideration.

items.title: OpenAI seeks to exclude book market study, citing funding ties to authors’ law firm
items.excerpt: The accuracy and funding of research claiming Gen AI causes market harm have become important questions in the consolidated lawsuits.

items.title: Publishing industry organizations release 2026 report on AI use
items.excerpt: Publishers report increased AI usage internally for marketing, metadata and title optimization, and admin work.

items.title: Can Better Wording Fix the “Made With AI” Problem? New 2026 Research Says It's Complicated
items.excerpt: Can better wording solve the “Made With AI” problem? Explore what new 2026 research reveals about AI-generated content, detection, trust, and communication.

items.title: Dartmouth Provost’s “AI Dependency” Sparks Backlash
items.excerpt: Some students and faculty are calling for the provost’s firing after he allegedly used generative AI to write professional articles. He’s admitted to using ChatGPT, but says it didn’t replace his own intellectual judgment or authorship.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Program Picks
items.excerpt: A sampling of the hundreds of outstanding panels and presentations on tap at the 2026 Frankfurter Buchmesse, which gets underway next week.

items.title: Claremont author faces criticism over AI art in new book
items.excerpt: Claremont Middle School hosted author Giulio Savo and his book "Directive Detectives: The Freedom Trail Directive," sparking debate over the use of AI in children's literature.

items.title: Is AI coming for audiobooks?
items.excerpt: AI companies like ElevenLabs and Spoken are angling for the fast-growing audiobook market. It remains to be seen if consumers will buy in.

items.title: New AI Model: GPT-6.1 Sol
items.excerpt: Barely a week after GPT-6 Sol, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol upgrade is now available inside Sudowrite for fiction writers.

items.title: Even More New Models: Sonnet 5.5, Gemini 3.7 & 3.8 and More
items.excerpt: Claude Sonnet 5.5 launched today, and Sudowrite has already made it available alongside new Gemini 3.7 and 3.8 models for fiction drafting.

items.title: Faster Chat, Better Rewrite & Printing
items.excerpt: Sudowrite's Chat responses are now twice as fast, with an improved Rewrite tool and new printing support for manuscripts.
